ios.desc:
Finally understand trigonometry.

Touch Trigonometry is the most intuitive way to learn the trigonometric functions. Instead of memorizing formulas, you'll see how sin, cos, tan, and the rest actually work—by touching and exploring a live unit circle and graph. Drag your finger around the circle and watch trig functions respond in real time. You'll be amazed at how quickly the "true meaning" of trigonometry becomes clear. Watch the graph on the right trace their values. In seconds, concepts that confused you for years will suddenly click. This app is great for students struggling with trigonometry or anyone looking for a refresher.

HOW IT WORKS

On the left: an interactive unit circle. Touch anywhere and drag to change the angle θ (theta). A triangle forms showing the relationships between the angle and the trig values. On the right: live graphs of all six trig functions. As you move the angle, dots trace along each curve showing the current value. Touch the graph side to control the angle from there too. It's bidirectional, immediate, and intuitive. No tutorial needed—just touch and explore. Users have told us that they never understood *why* the trig functions existed—until they used this app. From students to the math curious, Touch Trigonometry offers a truly intuitive way to understand one of the trickiest parts of geometry—at your fingertips!

FEATURES

• Interactive unit circle with touch control
• All 6 trig functions: sin, cos, tan, sec, csc, cot
• Live function graphs with real-time value tracking
• Bidirectional control (circle or graph)
• Right triangle overlay showing opposite/adjacent/hypotenuse
• Reference angle markers (30°, 45°, 60°, 90°, etc.)
• Switch between degrees and radians
• Snap-to-reference-angles mode
• Pinch to zoom the graph
• Colorblind-friendly color palette
• Clean dark theme, no distractions
• No ads, no account required

WHO IT'S FOR

• High school & college students learning trig
• Teachers demonstrating concepts in class
• Engineers & scientists refreshing fundamentals
• Anyone who was told to "just memorize SOHCAHTOA"
• Visual learners who need to see it to get it

FREE FEATURES

• Full unit circle interaction
• Sine visualization
• Triangle overlay
• Degree/radian switching
• All UI customization options

UNLOCK EVERYTHING (One-Time Purchase)

• One-time purchase for lifetime access to all paid features
• Cosine, tangent, secant, cosecant, cotangent
• All future paid features

quotes.text:
I started to teach myself to code around 15 years ago. At the time I was working service industry jobs (restaurant kitchens, coffee shops) and desperate to change my career and life.

Around that time there was a new thing called <canvas> available in HTML5 that you could use to render graphics in web pages without plugins; despite my limited knowledge of tech and lack of coding skills, I knew I wanted to be a part of that.

Around that same time, I had also enrolled at the community college for night classes in math. I wanted to "work in tech" after all, so a mathematics brush-up seemed wise. I had always struggled with math. But now that I was both incentivized to learn it, I found myself facing a familiar terror: trigonometry.

The other students, just out of high school, seemed to know this stuff. I was simply confused. The same frustration I had felt in high school returned: No one could clearly answer why this stuff worked. Why did we need a "sine" function?

So I decided to combine my struggles and make them into a single creative project: I would code a way to visualize and understand the trig functions - and in so doing, I would learn trigonometry and HTML5.

I called it "Touch Trigonometry" and the idea was simple: You move your mouse, and the visualization of the trig functions would update. There would be a unit circle showing the angle. There would be a graph showing the plots. As a kinesthetic learner, I theorized that if I could simply "play with trigonometry" …
